context: Normal QQ plot with 95% pointwise confidence envelope for a skewed mixture distribution (80% N(0,1) + 20% shifted normal), with an inset histogram showing the distribution vs. normal fit
first_impression: Statistically rigorous QQ plot with correctly computed delta-method confidence bands and data-driven symmetric axes, let down by a hardcoded inset histogram domain and a metadata mismatch between the source note (N(2.5, 0.8)) and the actual code (N(3.5, 0.6)).
what_works: Main plot axes use fully data-driven symmetric domain computed from d3.max over all quantiles and band boundaries; confidence band SE formula sqrt(p*(1-p)/n)/f(z) is mathematically correct, and outside-envelope points are correctly identified and color-encoded.
what_doesnt: Inset histogram domain is hardcoded at [-3.5, 3.5] and will silently clip extreme standardized values visible in the main plot; source note labels the shifted component as N(2.5, 0.8) but the code generates N(3.5, 0.6), a factual mismatch that undermines trust in the annotation.
